title: अंश ५ · अध्याय २२

items.text:
जरासन्घसुते कंस उपयेमे महाबलः ।
अस्ति प्राप्तिञ्च मैत्रेय!तयोर्भर्त्तृहनं हरिम् ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
jarāsanghasute kaṃsa upayeme mahābalaḥ |
asti prāptiñca maitreya!tayorbharttṛhanaṃ harim || 1 ||

items.text:
उपेत्य मथुरां सोऽथ रुरोध मगधेखरः ।
अक्षौहिणीभिः सैन्यस्य त्रयोविंशतिभिर्वृतः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
upetya mathurāṃ so'tha rurodha magadhekharaḥ |
akṣauhiṇībhiḥ sainyasya trayoviṃśatibhirvṛtaḥ || 3 ||

items.text:
निष्कम्याल्पपरीवारावुभौ राम-जनार्द्दनौ ।
युयुधातौ समं तस्य बलिनौ बलिसैनिकैः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
niṣkamyālpaparīvārāvubhau rāma-janārddanau |
yuyudhātau samaṃ tasya balinau balisainikaiḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
ततो बलश्व कृष्णश्व चक्राते मतिमुत्तमाम् ।
आयुधानां पुराणानामादाने मुनिसत्तम ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
tato balaśva kṛṣṇaśva cakrāte matimuttamām |
āyudhānāṃ purāṇānāmādāne munisattama || 5 ||

items.text:
अनन्तरं हरेः शाङ्ग तूणौ चाक्षयसायकौ ।
आकाशादागतौ वीर!तथा कौमोदकी गदा ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
anantaraṃ hareḥ śāṅga tūṇau cākṣayasāyakau |
ākāśādāgatau vīra!tathā kaumodakī gadā || 6 ||

items.text:
हलञ्च बलभद्रस्य गगनादागतं कवे !
मनसोऽभिमतं विप्र!सौनन्दं मुसलं तथा ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
halañca balabhadrasya gaganādāgataṃ kave !
manaso'bhimataṃ vipra!saunandaṃ musalaṃ tathā || 7 ||

items.text:
ततो युद्धे पराजित्य ससैन्यं मगधाधिपम् ।
पुरीं विविशतुर्वीरावुभौ राम-जनार्द्दनौ ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
tato yuddhe parājitya sasainyaṃ magadhādhipam |
purīṃ viviśaturvīrāvubhau rāma-janārddanau || 8 ||

items.text:
जते तस्मिन् सुदुर्वृत्ते जरासन्धे महामुने !
जीवमाने गते कृष्णस्तं नामन्यत निर्ज्जितम् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
jate tasmin sudurvṛtte jarāsandhe mahāmune !
jīvamāne gate kṛṣṇastaṃ nāmanyata nirjjitam || 9 ||

items.text:
पुनरप्याजगामाथ जरासन्धो बलान्वितः ।
जितश्व राम-कृष्णाभ्यामपक्रान्तो द्रिजोत्तम ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
punarapyājagāmātha jarāsandho balānvitaḥ |
jitaśva rāma-kṛṣṇābhyāmapakrānto drijottama || 10 ||

items.text:
दश चाष्टौ च संग्रामानेवमत्यन्तदुर्म्मदः ।
यदुभिर्मागधो राजा चक्र कृष्णापुरोगमैः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
daśa cāṣṭau ca saṃgrāmānevamatyantadurmmadaḥ |
yadubhirmāgadho rājā cakra kṛṣṇāpurogamaiḥ || 11 ||

items.text:
सर्व्वेष्वेतेषु युद्धेषु यादवैः स पराजितः ।
अपक्रान्तो जरासन्धः स्वल्पसैन्यैर्बलाधिकः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
sarvveṣveteṣu yuddheṣu yādavaiḥ sa parājitaḥ |
apakrānto jarāsandhaḥ svalpasainyairbalādhikaḥ || 12 ||

items.text:
तदू बल यादवानां तैरर्ज्जितं यदनेकशः ।
तत्तु सन्निधिमाहात्म्यं विष्णोरंशस्य चक्रिणः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
tadū bala yādavānāṃ tairarjjitaṃ yadanekaśaḥ |
tattu sannidhimāhātmyaṃ viṣṇoraṃśasya cakriṇaḥ || 13 ||

items.text:
मनुष्यधर्म्मशीलस्य लीला सा जगतः पतेः ।
अस्त्रणयनेकरूपाणि यदरातिषु मुञ्चति ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
manuṣyadharmmaśīlasya līlā sā jagataḥ pateḥ |
astraṇayanekarūpāṇi yadarātiṣu muñcati || 14 ||

items.text:
मनसैव जगत्सृष्टिं संहारञ्च करोति यः ।
तस्यारिपक्षक्षपणे कोऽयमुद्यमविस्तरः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
manasaiva jagatsṛṣṭiṃ saṃhārañca karoti yaḥ |
tasyāripakṣakṣapaṇe ko'yamudyamavistaraḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
तथापि यो मनुष्याणां धर्म्मस्तमनुवर्त्तते ।
कुर्व्वने बलवता सन्धिं हीनैर्युद्धं करोत्यसौ ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
tathāpi yo manuṣyāṇāṃ dharmmastamanuvarttate |
kurvvane balavatā sandhiṃ hīnairyuddhaṃ karotyasau || 16 ||

items.text:
साम चोपप्रदानञ्च तथा भेदं प्रदर्शयन् ।
करोति दण्डपातञ्च क्बचिदेव पलायनम् ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
sāma copapradānañca tathā bhedaṃ pradarśayan |
karoti daṇḍapātañca kbacideva palāyanam || 17 ||

items.text:
मनुष्यदेहिनां चेष्टामित्येवमनुवर्त्ततः ।
लीला जगतूपतेस्तस्य च्छन्दतः सम्प्रवर्त्तते ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
manuṣyadehināṃ ceṣṭāmityevamanuvarttataḥ |
līlā jagatūpatestasya cchandataḥ sampravarttate || 18 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—The mighty Kansa had married the two daughters of Jarāsandha, one named Asti, the other Prāpti. Jarāsandha was king of Magadha, and a very powerful prince, who, when he heard that Krishna had killed his son-in-law, was much incensed, and, collecting a large force, marched against Mathura, determined to put the Yādavas and Krishna to the sword. Accordingly he invested the city with three and twenty numerous divisions of his forces. Rāma and Janārddana sallied from the town with a slender, but resolute force, and fought bravely with the armies of Magadha. The two youthful leaders prudently resolved to have recourse to their ancient weapons, and accordingly the bow of Hari, with two quivers filled with exhaustless arrows and the mace called Kaumodaki, and the ploughshare of Balabhadra, as well as the club Saunanda, descended at a wish from heaven. Armed with these weapons, they speedily discomfited the king of Magadha and his hosts, and re-entered the city in triumph.

Although the wicked king of Magadha, Jarāsandha, was defeated, yet Krishna knew that whilst he escaped alive he was not subdued; and in fact, he soon returned with a mighty force, and was again forced by Rāma and Krishna to fly. Eighteen times did the haughty prince of Magadha renew his attack upon the Yādavas, headed by Krishna; and was as often defeated and put to the rout by them, with very inferior numbers. That the Yādavas were not overpowered by their foes, was owing to the present might of the portion of the discus-armed Vishnu. It was the pastime of the lord of the universe, in his capacity of man, to launch various weapons against his enemies; for what effort of power to annihilate his foes could be necessary to him, whose fiat creates and destroys the world? But as subjecting himself to human customs, he formed alliances with the brave, and engaged in hostilities with the base. He had recourse to the four devices of policy, or negotiation, presents, sowing dissension, and chastisement; and sometimes even betook himself to flight. Thus imitating the conduct of human beings, the lord of the world pursued at will his sports.
